title: Distribution Templates: the 2x2 Grid
quickIdea: Every balls-into-boxes question is classified on two axes - objects distinct or identical, boxes distinct or identical - and each cell has exactly one method.
remember: DODB (distinct objects, distinct boxes): k^n if boxes may be empty; onto case k! S(n,k).
IODB (identical objects, distinct boxes): C(n+k-1, k-1); if every box needs at least one, C(n-1, k-1).
DOIB (distinct objects, identical boxes): S(n,k), Stirling second kind; sum over k if empty boxes allowed.
IOIB (identical objects, identical boxes): p(n) into at most k parts; no closed formula, enumerate.
Default rule: if the question names no boxes, groups or teams, the boxes are identical.

example.prompt: 3 distinct balls into 2 distinct boxes, empty allowed.
example.work: Each ball picks a box independently: 2^3.

gateAngle: Almost every GATE distribution question is decided by this grid plus one sentence of wording. GATE 2022 Q.32 (7) is IOIB; GATE 2015 Set 3 Q.5 (15) is IODB; GATE 2003 Q.34 is IODB with a lower bound.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: 'Distribute 6 identical chocolates among 3 children.' Which template, and why not DODB?
variations.why: Chocolates are identical (they are the same object repeated) and children are labelled, so it is identical objects into distinct boxes. DODB would need the chocolates to be distinguishable, giving 3^6 = 729.

trap.what: Assuming boxes are labelled because they are mentioned.
trap.why: Naming the containers is not labelling them. 'Split into 3 groups' with no names means identical boxes.
trap.counterexample: 6 identical balls into 3 identical bins = 7 (partitions of 6 into at most 3 parts), while into 3 distinct bins it is C(8,2) = 28.

check.question: 4 distinct balls into 2 identical non-empty boxes - how many ways?
check.explanation: S(4,2) = 7: the boxes are unlabelled, so {1,2,3}|{4} is the same distribution as {4}|{1,2,3}.
